extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent practitioners (agents/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner checklist for preparing, filing, and handling Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 in U.S. patent applications, including content, timing, copies, translations, examiner consideration, and treatment in continuing and national stage proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English document requirement (concise explanation or translation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-English documents cited in an IDS, a concise explanation of the relevance as presently understood by the individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) must be provided unless a complete English translation is provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-English documents that are cited, provide (a) a concise explanation of the relevance as presently understood by the designated individual, unless a complete translation is provided; and/or (b) a written English-language translation of the portion cited if the translation is within the possession, custody, or control of, or is readily available to, any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of translation when translation is controlled
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the translation is required if a written English-language translation of a non-English document, or portion thereof, is within the possession, custody, or control of, or is readily available to, any individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the translating party possesses or controls a translation, submit a copy of that translation with the IDS (see the possession/custody/control language above).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required for each U.S. patent listed
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. patent listed in an information disclosure statement must be identified by inventor, patent number, and issue date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include inventor name(s), the patent number, and the issue date exactly as on the patent to ensure proper identification and OCR processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required for each U.S. patent application publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. patent application publication listed must be identified by applicant, patent application publication number, and publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide applicant name(s), the publication number, and the publication date for each U.S. patent application publication listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required for each U.S. application listed
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. application listed in an information disclosure statement must be identified by the inventor, application number, and filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List inventor name(s), application number, and filing date for pending U.S. applications cited in the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required for foreign patents/published foreign applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Each foreign patent or published foreign patent application listed must be identified by the country or patent office which issued or published it, an appropriate document number, and the publication date indicated on the patent or published application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide country/patent office, document number (including kind code where applicable), and publication/issue date for foreign documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required for publications (non-patent literature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each publication listed in an IDS must be identified by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages of the publication, date, and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sufficient bibliographic detail (publisher, author, title, pages, date, place) so the publication is unambiguously identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative disclosures exception
rubrics_metrics.description: When disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of the patents or publications may be submitted without copies of the others, provided it is stated that the other patents or publications are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting only one copy because others are cumulative, explicitly state which other references are cumulative to justify omission of their copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required even if previously submitted (subject to limited exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any patent, publication, pending U.S. application or other information listed in an IDS is required to be provided even if previously submitted to, or cited by, the Office in an earlier application, unless the earlier application is properly identified in the IDS and is relied on for an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120 and the earlier IDS complied with 37 CFR 1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume prior filing obviates copies; only rely on a prior application where (1) it is properly identified and (2) the prior IDS complied with the content rules—otherwise resubmit copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS not permitted in provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs) are not permitted in provisional applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because provisional applications receive no substantive examination, any IDS filed in a provisional will be returned or destroyed at the Office's option (see 37 CFR 1.51(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure for nonprovisional applications (37 CFR 1.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: In nonprovisional applications under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), applicants and individuals substantively involved with preparation/prosecution have a duty to submit information material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56; 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 provide the mechanism to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the IDS procedures to fulfill the duty of disclosure; submit information so the examiner can evaluate relevance to claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties (individuals not covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 37 CFR 1.97/1.98; third parties may submit patents and publications under 37 CFR 1.99 in applications published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b), or may file a protest under 37 CFR 1.291 for unpublished pending applications prior to mailing of a notice of allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties wishing the Office to consider information should either submit under the narrow 1.99 procedures for published applications or provide information to the applicant for inclusion in an IDS; improper IDS filings by third parties will be discarded before forwarding to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filing does not equal representation of a search or materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an IDS shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made, nor as an admission that the information cited is, or is considered to be, material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS is procedural and for providing examiner access to information; applicants retain separate duties and positions regarding searches and materiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligation to consider compliant IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the minimum requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 are met, the examiner has an obligation to consider the information; consideration means treating the documents in the same manner as other documents in Office search files while conducting a search in a proper field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will mark citations to indicate consideration (initials adjacent to citations) or use the alternative electronic signature method described; consideration does not require the item to be prior art, only that it be examined similarly to search-file documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner marking and alternative electronic signature method
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners indicate consideration by initialing adjacent to citation entries; alternatively, examiners may stamp each page 'All references considered except where lined through' with electronic initials and include an electronic signature on the final page; examiners will strike through each citation not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of examiner initials or the stamped phrase with electronic initials signifies that the information has been considered to the extent of an Office search-file consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliant IDS handling by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Information submitted to the Office that does not comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 will not be considered by the Office but will be placed in the application file; the examiner should draw a line through citations not considered and inform applicant of reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should explicitly indicate non-considered citations and inform applicant (e.g., using form paragraphs 6.49–6.49.09) of the reasons why a citation was not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple IDS filings allowed if each complies
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple information disclosure statements may be filed in a single application, and they will be considered provided each is in compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each IDS submission is evaluated independently for compliance; ensure each meets content and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO/SB/08A and 08B forms encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of form PTO/SB/08A and 08B ('Information Disclosure Statement') is encouraged as a means to provide the required list of information as set forth in 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms provide separate sections for U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications, a column for examiner initials, and are updated by the Office to reflect requirements—use to facilitate compliance and processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-related requirements for filing an IDS (37 CFR 1.97)
rubrics_metrics.description: IDS filing is subject to time-based rules in 37 CFR 1.97: e.g., for national applications (not CPAs) file within 3 months of filing or before first Office action on the merits, whichever is later; for national stage applications file within 3 months of entry into national stage or before first Office action; for RCEs and CPAs before first Office action on the merits; IDSs filed after payment of the issue fee will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different time windows trigger different required statements or fees (e.g., 1.97(e) statement or 1.17(p) fee). IDSs filed after certain events may still be considered only if accompanied by the appropriate statements/fees; otherwise they will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content/format requirements for the IDS listing (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The IDS listing must follow 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1): (A) a specified format/identification for each page of an IDS and U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications listed separately from other documents; (B) a column that provides space next to each document for the examiner's initials; and (C) a heading that identifies the list as an Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each page should clearly identify the application number (if known). Separation of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications facilitates OCR and electronic retrieval; if not using PTO forms, ensure separation and the required columns/heading are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identification details for listed citations (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) subitems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific identification required: (i) U.S. patents by patent number, issue date and inventor(s); (ii) U.S. patent application publications by publication number, publication date and inventor(s); (iii) pending U.S. applications by application number, filing date and inventor(s); (iv) foreign patent documents by document number (including kind code), country and publication/issue date; (v) non-patent literature by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, and date and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact identifying elements listed above for each type of citation so the Office can properly process and retrieve the documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies requirement for cited documents (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies must be provided for: (a) each cited foreign patent document; (b) each cited non-patent literature publication or the portion which caused it to be listed; (c) each cited U.S. pending application that is not stored in IFW; (d) all information cited (e.g., an affidavit or Office action), other than the specification, including claims and drawings of a pending U.S. application; and (e) all other cited information or the portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When listing a document you must attach a legible copy of the required portion; failure to provide required copies causes the IDS to be non-compliant and the items not to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for non-English document submission (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-English documents, provide either a concise relevance explanation by the designated knowledgeable individual or an English translation copy if the translation is in that individual's possession/custody/control; one of these is required under 37 CFR 1.98(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit untranslated non-English documents without the concise explanation or translation described—otherwise they may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner actions after reviewing IDS for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing the IDS for compliance with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, examiner actions include: considering properly submitted information in the same manner as Office search-file documents; initialing the blank column next to citations or using the alternative electronic signature method; drawing a line through citations not considered and informing applicant why; writing 'not considered' if none comply; signing and dating the bottom of the IDS listing (or using the electronic method); and ensuring a signed/date copy is entered into the file and mailed to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For e-IDS, use the e-IDS icon to consider cited U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications; follow the stated notification procedures (form paragraphs) when informing applicants that citations were not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS treatment in continued prosecution / continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a continuing application that claims benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 to a parent application, it is generally unnecessary to resubmit an IDS listing prior art cited by the examiner in the parent application unless applicant desires the information to be printed on the patent; the examiner of the continuing application will consider information considered by the Office in the parent application. There are distinctions for CPAs, continuations, divisionals, continuation-in-part, and national stage international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CPAs (37 CFR 1.53(d)) and some continuations, previously considered information will be part of the file and need not be resubmitted; for other continuing applications, resubmission may be required to ensure consideration if the information was not previously considered. For international applications designating the U.S., include documents cited in the international search report if you want them considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission formatting and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: If resubmitting a listing of information, applicant should submit a new listing that complies with the format requirements in 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1); applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting a list that includes copies of PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms from other applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reuse form copies from other applications because prior examiner initials and other application numbers can confuse the record and leave no space for the current examiner's initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage (PCT) handling of cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: In a national stage application, the examiner will consider documents cited in the international search report when Form PCT/DO/EO/903 indicates that both the search report and the copies of the documents are present in the national stage file; in such cases the examiner should indicate in the first Office action that the information has been considered. The references in the Search Report are not an IDS complying with 37 CFR 1.98 unless copies and a separate list are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant wants references printed on the patent, a separate listing (preferably on PTO/SB/08A and 08B) must be filed within the set period; otherwise the Search Report citations may not be listed on any resulting patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason for separation of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) requires that U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications be listed separately from citations of other documents to permit the Office to obtain U.S. patent numbers and publication numbers by OCR from scanned documents and make them electronically available to examiners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the separate sections (as provided on PTO forms) to facilitate OCR, electronic retrieval, and examiner searching; failure to separate may impede processing.
